water.name: Land
water.rule: At least 4 of the hex's 7 sample points (centre + 6) fall on a Galician concello or on a neighbouring land outline (Asturias, León, Zamora, Portugal), unless the centre is sea and the elevation mean is at or below sea level, or at least half its samples are (the rías stay water).

water.name: Ocean
water.rule: Sea deeper than 200 m and not next to land.

water.name: Coast
water.rule: Sea next to a land hex, or shallower than 200 m (ETOPO1 mean; the Atlantic and Cantabrian coasts).

water.name: Lake
water.rule: At least 3 of the 7 sample points on an OpenStreetMap reservoir or lake (≥ 2 km²), above sea level; or a water hex (most of its points off land) with lake points that outnumber sea points, or above sea level.

relief.name: Flat
relief.rule: Elevation standard deviation inside the hex under 31 m.

relief.name: Mountains
relief.rule: Elevation standard deviation ≥ 85 m, or mean elevation ≥ 900 m.

relief.name: Peaks
relief.rule: Mean elevation ≥ 1,200 m (high mountain: Trevinca, Courel, Ancares).

cover.name: None
cover.rule: Water, foreign land, or no land-cover pixels.

cover.name: Deciduous forest
cover.rule: Forest (41+42+43) is the largest group and deciduous (41) the largest forest type.

cover.name: Conifer forest
cover.rule: Forest is the largest group and evergreen (42) the largest forest type.

cover.name: Mixed forest
cover.rule: Forest is the largest group and mixed (43) the largest forest type.

cover.name: Scrub & desert
cover.rule: Shrub/scrub (52) is the largest group: deserts, chaparral, sagebrush.

cover.name: Grassland
cover.rule: Grassland/herbaceous (71) plus developed open space (21: lawns, parks) is the largest group.

cover.name: Cropland
cover.rule: Cultivated crops (82) is the largest group.

cover.name: Wetland
cover.rule: Woody (90) plus emergent herbaceous (95) wetlands is the largest group.

cover.name: Urban
cover.rule: Developed low/medium/high intensity (22+23+24) is ≥ 15% of the hex's land, whatever else is there.

cover.name: Barren
cover.rule: Barren land (31: rock, sand, playa) is the largest group.

cover.name: Ice & snow
cover.rule: Perennial ice/snow (12) is the largest group.

notes.water: IGN municipal outlines (Galicia) and provincial outlines (Asturias, León, Zamora) come from one service, so borders meet; Portugal is Natural Earth 1:10m. The coast is the concellos' coastline. A water hex whose centre lies on a land outline, whose elevation mean is above sea level (and under half of its samples below it) becomes land when at least 4 of its 6 neighbours are land, or when it touches both Galician and foreign land; it takes the neighbours' majority owner. A hex whose centre is off every outline is sea: the elevation of the sea is too coarse to overrule the coastline. The rías stay water when the hex centre is sea and its mean is at or below sea level, or at least half of its samples are. A sea hex's elevation is the mean of its samples (ETOPO1, interpolated) below sea level (its water depth). Reservoirs and lakes of at least 2 km² (OpenStreetMap) are water where at least 3 of a hex's 7 sample points fall on them.
notes.relief: From IGN MDT 200 m samples (~0.15 × 0.2 km, about 85 per hex) with altitude ≥ -5 m, so rías and sea floor don't count; all samples are used if none qualify. Water hexes are always flat.
notes.cover: From ESA WorldCover 2021 (10 m), sampled on a 0.2 km lattice inside each Galician hex (about 65 points). Open water (11) and no-data pixels are ignored; shares are of the remaining land points, rounded to whole percent, and the urban threshold is applied to the rounded developed share. WorldCover does not tell oak from pine or eucalyptus, so all tree cover is mixed forest, and WorldCover's grassland (mostly Galician prados) is read as pasture. Foreign hexes have cover 0 (none).
